description: Crystal Lake Dam lake-rise model. Parameters from the Hydrologic Reference (June 2026): Dinicola 1990 Till Forest HSPF set + 2007 HEC-HMS geometry. US customary units throughout (inches, cfs, acres, acre-feet, feet, hours).

hspf.groundwater_comment: Active-groundwater / intermediate-subsurface limb. AGWRC_per_day=0.97 -> half-life ~23 d (hourly 0.97**(1/24)=0.998732). This is a deliberate MODERATE store, not the Ecology Till nominal 0.996 (~173-d half-life): at 173 d the store returns almost nothing within a multi-day event window, so soil drainage routed there was effectively lost to the near-term budget and the modeled lake drew down after rain while the gauge held. A 23-d store returns that water over weeks, which is what a till basin's sustained recession actually does. 0.97 sits inside the EPA Tech Note 6 typical band (0.92-0.99); revisit against gauge-derived recession (brief C/D.1). NOTE: a single lumped store still can't both sustain the moderate-storm recession AND keep the sharp Step 6 flood peak (same water, opposite timing) - a true two-timescale subsurface is the structural fix. KVARY_per_in=0.0 keeps the store LINEAR (Ecology Till is 0.5/in; enable later, brief D.5). DEEPFR=0.05 is the fraction of percolation permanently lost out of basin (the ONLY true sink); low end for a low-relief closed till basin (Wolock BFI=0.67). EPA ranges: AGWRC 0.85-0.999, KVARY 0.0-5.0, DEEPFR 0.0-0.50.
hspf.percolation_comment: Soil-bucket percolation to groundwater (brief B.2 option b, open question #3), active BELOW full saturation so light rain produces realistic baseflow recharge instead of nothing. perc = PERC_coeff * INFILT_in_per_hr * INFILD * (SM/LZSN)**INFEXP per hour. This is the ONLY groundwater recharge path; saturation-excess overflow (SM>LZSN) routes 100% to fast interflow (slow matrix drainage -> slow store; storm excess -> fast store). INFILD=2.0, INFEXP=2.0 are HSPF Till values; (SM/LZSN)**2 strongly suppresses drainage when dry. PERC_coeff=0.20 (2x the HSPF nominal 0.1) is CALIBRATED to the 2026-06-12 gauge recession: 66 h after a 2.89 in wet spell the lake was still rising at ~0.2 in/day, implying ~3.7 cfs sustained baseflow. At 0.1 the model delivered only ~2.5 cfs and the lake fell; 0.20 reproduces the ~3.7 cfs and the rising trend. It also controls the POST-RAIN dynamics: enough percolation that the soil keeps feeding the store for days after rain (so baseflow is still building, lake rising), which is why the trend sign needs PERC, not the seed. COST: percolation drains the bucket at saturation, so the Step 6 flood peak drops to 342.78 ft (still within 343.1+/-0.5, but margin to the lower bound is ~0.18 ft) -- this is near the practical ceiling; larger baseflow without hurting the flood peak needs the two-timescale subsurface (structural). CALIBRATION FOLLOW-UP: confirm across seasons / a true dry-down and against the Wolock BFI~0.67 (brief C/D.1).

datum.comment: Maps the HA lake-depth sensor reading to absolute elevation: abs = reading + sensor_to_absolute_offset_ft. PROVISIONAL (open item #2): the doc's +339.0 is the staff/WQ frame, but sensor.crystal_lake_depth has a DIFFERENT zero. 338.375 is cross-checked from the existing HA helper crystal_lake_threshold_summer_normal=1.3 (depth) corresponding to the doc's 3-log summer pool 339.675 ft (i.e. 339.675-1.3). Independently corroborated: a hindcast from the June seasonal default lands at ~339.68 ft for the current 1.36 reading. CONFIRM with a field tape-down before trusting absolute thresholds.

primary.comment: soffit_elev_ft (opening top) INFERRED from the rated 110 cfs @ 342 ft taken as the full-flow point: ~3.2 ft above the 338.8 ft sill, 'somewhat taller' than the aux. Above it the opening drowns and flow follows a submerged-orifice (sqrt-head) law. ESTIMATE pending a field measurement of the primary opening. seam_bottom_elev_ft = bare sill 338.8: seams leak from here up to the active stop-log crest.

auxiliary.comment: soffit_elev_ft = bridge underside, measured 2.5 ft above the zero-stop-log datum (338.8 ft) -> 341.3 ft absolute; the flow opening is ~1.3 ft above the 340.0 ft crest. Drowns ~0.9 ft below the 342.2 ft dam crest, so the aux is orifice-limited (flow nearly plateaus) before the dam overtops. seam_bottom_elev_ft = 338.8: the aux stop-log stack runs 338.8 -> 340.0 (same base as the primary, per the 2.5 ft height measured from that datum), so its 7.5 ft of seam leaks whenever the lake is above 338.8.

overtopping.comment: Once the lake exceeds the dam crest (342.2 ft, =thresholds.dam_crest) the whole ~60 ft crest spills as one broad-crested weir, Q = 2.6 * 60 * (h-342.2)**1.5, added on top of the two spillway legs. weir_coeff 2.6 is a standard broad-crested coefficient (US customary); tune once a real overtopping event or a survey of the crest profile is available. This relief caps the modeled rise above the crest: the Step 6 saturated anchor peaks ~0.2 ft lower than the spillway-only model (still within the 343.1 +/-0.5 ft target).

leakage.comment: Seepage through the stop-log seams of EVERY leg, continuously: per leg = cfs_per_ft2 * crest_length_ft * submerged_seam_height, where submerged_seam_height = min(lake, crest) - seam_bottom (capped at the full stack). Present at the bare-board dry recession AND underneath water spilling over the top. cfs_per_ft2=0.040 puts the combined primary (10 ft) + aux (7.5 ft) seam leakage at the summer dry equilibrium at ~0.6 cfs (down from an earlier 0.0557 -> ~0.8 cfs, which over-attributed dry-season outflow now that a standing baseflow inflow is modeled). Stays inside the cfs_low/high=0.5-2.0 bound (Reference 4.4a). Still holds the 72 h recession anchor in the observed 339.6-339.8 ft band. First-order (linear in submerged height, shared coefficient across legs); needs a real dry spell to calibrate the split and the head dependence.

seasonal_sm_default_frac_of_lzsn.comment: Fraction of LZSN to seed SM by month when insufficient rainfall history exists for replay (Reference 1.5). Dry late-summer -> near 0; near-saturated Dec-Apr -> ~1.0.

seasonal_agw_default_in.comment: Standing active-groundwater storage (inches over the watershed) to seed by month, so the slow store isn't unphysically empty at the start of every prediction (the short trailing-rainfall hindcast can't charge it). Values are a seasonal standing baseflow target converted to storage via S_agw = Q / (1 - AGWRC**(1/24)) at AGWRC=0.97: roughly Q ~= 1.8 cfs midwinter down to ~0.35 cfs late-summer, consistent with recharge ~13-23% of precip under forested till (Bauer & Mastin 1997) and the wet-Nov-Mar / dry-Jul-Sep PNW pattern. (Inches are smaller than they would be for the old 173-d store because a faster store needs less storage for the same baseflow; recompute this table if AGWRC changes.) PROVISIONAL placeholder: tune against gauge-derived dry-spell baseflow and the Wolock BFI~0.67 (brief C/D.1). Verified the summer value keeps the 3-log dry-equilibrium anchor in 339.6-339.8 ft.

uncertainty.comment: Lead-time-dependent multiplicative (log-normal) precip error. median = forecast; low/high are the ~10th/90th pct of (actual/forecast) -- the 80% interval -- and are ASYMMETRIC (fatter high tail: heavy events are biased low, the dangerous direction for EAP thresholds). Grounded in WPC QPF threat-score decay and global precip-overlap skill (see docs/forecast-uncertainty.md). Cool-season PNW frontal/AR regime is the favorable baseline; summer convection widens the band and lowers confidence via season_spread_factor. PLACEHOLDER until site forecast-vs-gauge pairs are logged and fit (spec 3.5).
